title: Missing CSRF Token Protection on Form
description: The /addbook form does not implement CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) token protection. The form accepts POST requests without validating a unique, per-request CSRF token. This allows attackers to craft malicious requests that, when clicked by legitimate users, will be executed with the user's context and permissions. The application contains no CSRF token field (checked for common names: csrf_token, _csrf_token, authenticity_token, __RequestVerificationToken) and no custom CSRF headers in responses.
impact: Attackers can perform CSRF attacks against users visiting malicious websites. For this application, attackers could: (1) craft malicious XML payloads and trick users into uploading them, (2) craft XXE payloads that exploit the application on behalf of the user, (3) upload malicious books to damage the database or retrieve sensitive information, and (4) perform unauthorized actions that the user is authenticated to perform. While this application has no authentication, in a real scenario with authenticated users, CSRF could lead to account compromise and unauthorized state-changing operations.
evidence:
POC Execution Results:
1. Form HTML Analysis: No CSRF token field detected in /addbook form HTML
2. Response Headers: No CSRF-related headers (X-CSRF-Token, X-XSRF-Token) detected
3. POST Request Test: 
   - Command: curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/addbook -d 'xml=<Book><Title>CSRF Test</Title></Book>'
   - Result: HTTP 200 OK - Request accepted and processed without any token validation
4. Form HTML Structure:
   <form action="/addbook" method="POST">
       <textarea name="xml" rows="20" cols="50"></textarea>
       <input type='submit' value='Parse'/>
   </form>
   (No hidden CSRF token input field present)
remediation:
1. Implement CSRF token validation on all state-changing forms (POST/PUT/DELETE):
   - Use Flask-WTF library: pip install flask-wtf
   - Initialize CSRF protection: from flask_wtf.csrf import CSRFProtect; csrf = CSRFProtect(app)
   - Add to template: {{ csrf_token() }} inside form

2. For each form, include hidden CSRF token input:
   <form method="POST">
       <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}"/>
       <textarea name="xml"></textarea>
   </form>

3. Implement SameSite cookie flag to prevent CSRF by default:
   - Set cookie SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax in Flask configuration
   - app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE'] = 'Lax'

4. For API endpoints, require custom headers (X-CSRF-Token) and validate them server-side

5. CSRF tokens should:
   - Be unique per user/session
   - Have reasonable expiration times
   - Be validated on server-side before processing requests
   - Be cryptographically random and sufficiently long

6. Consider implementing double-submit cookie pattern as fallback security mechanism
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control (CSRF), CWE-352 - Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), OWASP CSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet, RFC 7231 - Content-Type header specification
toolCallDescription: Documenting CSRF vulnerability in /addbook form with working POC demonstrating missing token protection
